description:
[Merchant] **Replace** a shop's whole delivery table. Whatever you do not send is removed, so read it first with `payware_shops_get_delivery` and send every row you want to keep. An empty `countries` list means "deliver anywhere, no fee".

**Endpoint:** PUT /shops/{shopCode}/delivery

Each row: `country` (ISO alpha-2), `currency`, `fee` and optionally `freeAbove`, all amounts decimal strings at the currency's payable scale (at most 15 significant and 15 integer digits). Rules: no two rows with the same country and currency, at most 250 rows, `fee` 0 or more, `freeAbove` above zero. A refusal is 400 `ERR_INVALID_DELIVERY_COUNTRY`, `ERR_INVALID_DELIVERY_SETTINGS` or `ERR_INVALID_AMOUNT_LENGTH` and nothing is saved.

**Read the answer.** It is the saved table and, when the table is not empty, `undeliverableProducts` (also on every read of the table, until resolved) (`productId`, `name`, `currency`): the shop's active shippable products whose currency has no row in it, so they can now be delivered nowhere. It is absent when there are none. The table is saved either way: tell the merchant, and add rows in those currencies if that was not the intent.

Needs a plan that can ship: Standard or Premium. A Basic (BSC) merchant is refused with 403 `ERR_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_CURRENT_USER_PLAN`. Changes are audit-logged.

countries.description: The complete table: one row per country and currency. Empty means deliver anywhere with no fee

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, e.g. BG (accepted in any case, returned upper case)

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of this row, e.g. EUR. A product is delivered only where its own currency has a row

fee.description: Delivery fee as a decimal string at the currency's payable scale, e.g. "5.00". 0 is free delivery

freeAbove.description: Optional: delivery is free when the goods total reaches this amount, e.g. "50.00". Above zero

useSandbox.description: Use the sandbox (the default) rather than production

name: payware_shops_set_delivery
